Hi guys! I've been asking a lot of questions recently and thought I should probably illustrate my ideas and give them away. I've been very busy designing an entirely different gun and getting the functional prototype working, but here is another one that I think just about anyone should be able to build.

The only catch is, I need some help with the actual dimensions. I work mostly with polymers and don't have a ton of experience with steels, so please give me any advice you can.

The .45 Long Colt AR Upper

So the main idea is to use steel plumbing pipe for the receiver tube, small pieces of scrap steel for the mounting-lugs, and some sheet metal for the mag well. Ideally one would use NPT tapered thread pipe to make fabricating and installing the suppressor easier.

The upper basic illustration.

The actual mag will be loaded in front of the stock magwell to allow for downward ejection of the brass. I think one could just follow Sten magazine dimensions and enlarge them by the same ratios as 9mm:.45lc.

Ejection will be facilitated by a cut in the top of bolt that will allow an ejector blade to ride within, stabilizing the bolt as well as ejecting the cartridge downward.

Shown here.

The bolt itself would be built up similarly to common 'expedient' bolt designs, save for a long hole bored through the center for an AR standard firing pin and a firing pin extension made of 8mm round spring steel.

The rear end of the bolt will interface with the stock buffer tube and buffer, simplifying the assembly process. Ideally the heavier bolt weight from the extension would dampen recoil. Or, God forbid that someone make an open-bolt version, lower the fire rate to make it more controllable.

Shown here.

I need some help with the exact dimensions and standardization of parts. Ideally we would be able to give a stranger a parts list and they could go to Home Depot to get everything. Not really sure how dimensions would work either, but I think this gun could be a lot of fun to make. Any ideas? Suggestions? I'd love it if some good folks got involved.
